title: Blowup domination detected by an ideal factorization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $J,K\subseteq R$ be finitely generated ideals with $\sqrt J=\sqrt K$, where $\sqrt H=\{x\in R:x^a\in H\text{ for some }a\geq1\}$. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $B_H=\operatorname{Bl}_H(X)$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup] for $H=J,K$. There exists an $X$-morphism $B_K\to B_J$ if and only if there exist an integer $n\geq1$ and a finitely generated ideal $L\subseteq R$ with $K^n=JL$.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed p.373: when V(J) is contained in V(J-prime), J <= J-prime iff J-prime^n = J K for some n > 0 and ideal K; equal-support specialization. proof.text: For a given morphism $f:B_K\to B_J$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, radical equality implies $K\subseteq\sqrt J$. Apply [lem-per-blowup-domination-colon-power]. With $C_d=(K^d:J)$ and $D_d=JC_d$, this gives for every $b\in K$ a positive $e_b$ with $b^{e_b}\in D_{e_b}$ in $R$.

The colon definition gives $D_d\subseteq K^d$ and $K^m C_d\subseteq C_{d+m}$, hence $K^mD_d\subseteq D_{d+m}$. Apply finite-generation induction to subideals $H\subseteq K$. For a singleton ideal $(b)$ the per-element relation supplies a positive $e$ with $(b)^e\subseteq D_e$. For a sum $H_1+H_2$, suppose $H_1^a\subseteq D_a$ and $H_2^b\subseteq D_b$. Expand $(H_1+H_2)^{a+b}$. Each term $H_1^iH_2^{a+b-i}$ has $i\geq a$ or $a+b-i\geq b$. In the first case it lies in $D_a K^{a+b-a}\subseteq D_{a+b}$, and in the second in $D_b K^{a+b-b}\subseteq D_{a+b}$. The binomial coefficient can only shrink an ideal. Thus for some $n\geq1$, $K^n\subseteq D_n$. The reverse inclusion gives $K^n=JC_n$. This is implemented by the private lemmas propagate_power, power_le_of_elementwise and factor_of_elementwise_colon.

proof.text: Finite coefficient truncation is proved by ideal-multiplication induction: if $x\in JC$, then $x$ lies in $JL_x$ for some finitely generated $L_x\subseteq C$. A pure product $jc$ uses $L_x=(c)$; a sum uses the sum of the two finite factors. Finite-generation induction on $H\subseteq JC$ combines these factors for all generators into one finitely generated $L\subseteq C$ with $H\subseteq JL$. Apply this with $H=K^n$ and $C=C_n$. Then $JL\subseteq JC_n=K^n$, so $K^n=JL$. The private finite_factor_of_mem_mul and finite_factor_of_fg_le_mul carry this Lean argument.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $K^n=JL$ with $n\geq1$ and $L$ finitely generated. On $B_K$, the extension of $K$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]; hence its $n$th power is generated by the $n$th power of that same regular generator. On each affine open of $B_K$, [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension] identifies the extensions with the ring ideals generated by $K,J,L$. Extension commutes with ideal products and powers because both are generated by the same finite products of images. Thus $(J\mathcal O_{B_K})(L\mathcal O_{B_K})=K^n\mathcal O_{B_K}$ is an effective Cartier ideal. Apply [lemma-nagata-ideal-invertible-product-factor] on these affine opens to conclude that $J\mathcal O_{B_K}$ is an effective Cartier ideal.

proof.text: Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] to the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I=\widetilde J$ of $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and to the structure morphism $t:B_K\to X$. Its hypothesis is that the extended ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{B_K}=J\mathcal O_{B_K}$ is invertible, that is, locally generated by a single non-zero-divisor; this is exactly the effective-Cartier property proved in step 7. The theorem gives a morphism $h:B_K\to\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ with $b_{X,\mathcal I}\circ h=t$. Since $X$ is affine, it is the terminal affine open of itself, so the colimit of local models defining $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ in [def-nagata-global-blowup] is the local model over $X$ itself, namely $B_J=\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal R_R(J)$ of [def-nagata-affine-blowup] with its structure map. Thus $h$ is an $X$-morphism $B_K\to B_J$. This proves the reverse implication and completes the equivalence. In the Lean comparison, first transport the ideal along the genuine ring isomorphism $R\simeq\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)$; functoriality of the affine blowup sends a ring isomorphism to a scheme isomorphism, with inverse obtained from the inverse ring map and the composition law. The chart inclusion over the top affine open is an isomorphism since its open range is the preimage of the whole base. Their composite $g_J:B_J\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{\widetilde J}(X)$ commutes with the structure maps. Pullback along the analogous $g_K$ supplies affine principalization, and the final lift is $h$ followed by $g_J^{-1}$. The private lemmas exists_global_comparison and hom_of_pow_factorization implement these identifications; no object is chosen in a definition from an unproved existence statement.
